subject: Acme POC: Evaluation plan, success criteria, and eval methodology alignment
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Acme POC: Evaluation plan, success criteria, and eval methodology alignment

Jordan - thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment before the PoC kicks off:

Summary of goals
- Reduce manual triage time for customer support by ~40% on Tier 1 tickets
- Maintain >= 92% accuracy on intent classification and >= 85% on suggested reply relevance (per your internal definition)

Proposed PoC structure (2 phases)
1) Offline evaluation (2 weeks) - we run your historical ticket sample through our inference pipeline, produce outputs, and grade with a shared rubric. Primary goal: validate model/quantization choice, prompt templates, and baseline metrics.
2) Shadow/online (2 weeks) - live shadowing in your staging environment with no user-facing changes; monitor latency, confidence calibration, and live-fail behavior. If metrics hold, proceed to a small pilot.

Owners & timeline
- Redwood: Dylan (sales) + Marissa (evals lead) + Neha (infra/config) - deliver offline eval results and rubric.
- Acme: Jordan (product owner) + procurement for contract sign-off.
- Proposed kickoff: week of Jul 19. Offline eval window: Jul 20-Jul 30. Shadow window: Aug 2-Aug 13.

Attachments: acme-poc-eval-plan-v1.pdf (POC plan + data checklist).

Questions / asks for you
1) Can you confirm the sample dataset size we agreed on (5k tickets, anonymized)?
2) Are the success thresholds above aligned with your stakeholders? If not, please propose.
3) Can procurement's contact be looped so we can circulate the SOW?

If this looks good I'll loop Marissa to drive the evaluation rubric and sample prompts.

Thanks - Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
dylan@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@acmecorp.com>

Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme POC: Evaluation plan, success criteria, and eval methodology alignment

Thanks, Dylan - this is helpful and matches what I heard on the call. A few clarifications from our side:

- Sample size: 5k anonymized tickets sounds right, but we'll confirm with engineering tomorrow (I expect small adjustments).
- Success thresholds: intent accuracy >=92% is fine; reply relevance we'd prefer >=87% if possible. We'll flag this with the support manager.
- Evaluation methodology: curious about the offline vs. online split. Would you recommend starting with offline only, or run a short shadow concurrently? Our infra team is tight next week so ideally offline first.

I'm looping procurement (cc) - can you send the SOW + pricing terms we discussed? Procurement will want a one-page summary for the request.

Jordan

jordan.blake@acmecorp.com

Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme POC: Evaluation plan, success criteria, and eval methodology alignment

Jordan - thanks for the quick reply and for looping procurement. Short answers to your questions and a bit more detail on why we recommend the two-phase approach:

Why offline first
- Faster to iterate on prompts, temperature, and ranking without impacting live latency or customers.
- Provides a reproducible baseline so we can make defensible model/quantization choices.
- Allows Marissa to run blinded grading across major ticket categories (billing, login, feature requests).

When to run shadowing
- We recommend starting shadowing only after the offline results meet thresholds (or show clear improvement). If your infra bandwidth is tight next week, we'll begin offline on Jul 20 and postpone shadowing until Aug 2 as proposed.

Deliverables we'll provide
- Offline eval report (per-category metrics + overall rubric)
- Grading spreadsheet: redwood-eval-rubric.xlsx
- Sample prompt set: sample-prompt-set.csv
- One-page SOW + pricing summary (attached draft).

Next steps
1) Confirm dataset size by Tue Jul 13 EOD.
2) Procurement: happy to provide one-pager + SOW - sending draft attached.
3) Marissa will follow up with grading rubric and sample prompts once dataset is confirmed.

Attachments (drafts): acme-poc-eval-plan-v1.pdf, redwood-eval-rubric.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@acmecorp.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme POC: Evaluation plan, success criteria, and eval methodology alignment

Jordan / Dylan - looping in the evals details so we can lock on a grading rubric quickly. Key points below and an initial pass at actionable grading buckets. I'll share the spreadsheet after we confirm dataset size.

Suggested grading rubric (offline)
- Intent classification: Exact match / fuzzy match / partial - weight 40%
- Reply relevance: human judge 0-3 scale (0: irrelevant, 3: directly usable) - weight 40%
- Safety & policy flags: binary pass/fail - auto-fail overrides - weight 20%

Acceptance thresholds (example)
- Weighted score >= 0.87 to pass.
- Per-category lower bounds: Billing >= 0.85, Login >= 0.88, Feature requests >= 0.80.

Offline vs online notes
- Offline grading will be blinded and randomized across judges to reduce bias. We recommend at least 3 judges for a 5k sample subset (we can stratify by ticket type).
- For online shadow we'll track additional metrics: latency P95, confidence calibration (expected vs observed accuracy by confidence bucket), and false positive rate for critical policy triggers.

Next steps from Marissa
- I will prepare redwood-eval-rubric.xlsx and a sample prompt set (sample-prompt-set.csv) by Wed Jul 14 EOD.
- Dylan: once dataset size is confirmed we'll request a secure transfer link and provide the data checklist.

Thanks - Marissa
